scope.frame: the weave's fibre (B1642's zero modes), given Lambda; the surface frame where covariance under the moves is invoked; B1600's convention for the moves and lifts
scope.object: the zero modes' pairing triplet v(z, tau) = c_r th_r(0) th_r(z)/th_1(z) at every point of the fibre, its residue at the puncture, and the moves' action on it
scope.hypotheses: premise P1 (an even, single-point Higgs) confines couplings to the four fixed points and is tested by no cell; the punctured, parabolic bulk statement and the legality of half-period fields (W60, P-108) are owed; leading order only

claim_one_line: WHERE A HIGGS CAN COUPLE THE ZERO MODES (sealed 6d6f7f660; PROVED -- every cell holds as sealed): no flat or harmonic Higgs couples the fibre's zero modes in the bulk (every non-zero pairing carries a non-trivial 2-torsion character, U2 to 5e-30); the pairing triplet v(z) = c_r th_r(0) th_r(z)/th_1(z) is isotropic at EVERY point (a theta identity, U3a to 7e-31), so at one tau a Higgs at any single point leaves one generation massless -- B1649's zero is a property of a single point, not of the puncture; the moves carry the triplet exactly at every point (U4: L, tau -> tau + 1, as Ad(g_L)^-1 and R, tau -> tau/(tau + 1), as Ad(g_R), with no Klein element, to 2e-16 at all four fixed points; a swapped-matrix control fails, 0.9976), and only the half-periods' triplets (0, -1, i), (i, 0, 1), (i, -1, 0) are independent of tau (U3b, with the puncture and generic points as controls); the lifts generate O, irreducible on M, and modulo the Klein group only the four real body diagonals are covariant (U5), so a covariant constant Higgs direction gives no hierarchy (B1646). Step 4 answered: under premise P1 (an even, single-point Higgs; tested by no cell) the covariant loci among the fixed points are the puncture, the half-period orbit, or both (surface frame), any of them at one tau -- the puncture is not forced, and P-129's first premise is a choice. Owed: the half-period orbit's mass structure (tau-independent triplets; to the frame tribunal, P-136), the legality of half-period fields (W60, P-108), the parabolic bulk statement, the odd Higgs's pair couplings. Corrected twice before the seal, both disclosed. [Scoped at S126 (2026-10-14) by the seats' answers (ADDENDUM_2026-10-14_the_seats_answers.md): 'the puncture is not forced' holds for point Higgs fields (premise P1); for a bulk Higgs carrying parity, the SM seat's section 107 reading (Stokes; by hand, not yet checked on main) forces the puncture as the locus at the price of one end datum; chat1: a thread restricts the locus no more than the surface frame (by B1602's classes), and a half-period value carries one unit of weight more than the residue, a phase debt when the two are mixed.] 0 of 19.
